newsitem.title: HONG KONG: RESEARCH ALERT - Salomon sees downside to H shares.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Salomon sees downside to H shares.

text.p: Salomon Brothers cut profit forecasts on three Hong Kong-listed mainland China (H share) companies and maintained its recommendation of underperform on all the H share counters the U.S. brokerage covered.
Pitzi Lau, an analyst of Salomon, said she did not agree that share prices of the 21 H-share companies had bottomed out despite their brief rebound in mid-August.

"If you look at Luoyang Glass, the company is facing more competition and at the moment I still have my concern at the chemical companies," she said, adding there was no concrete signs of an uptrend in the chemical sector.
Salomon currently covers five H share companies -- Luoyang Glass Co Ltd, Tsingtao Brewery Co Ltd, Yizheng Chemical Fibre Co Ltd, Shanghai Petrochemical Co Ltd and Jilin Chemical Industrial Co Ltd.
It cut profit estimates for at least three companies following disappointing interim results released last month.
The brokerage revised down Luoyang Glass' annual earnings forecast to 39 million yuan from 63 million for the year after it posted an 87 percent drop of its interim net.
It also cut 1997 annual profit forecast of the company to 43 million from 77 million, largely due to the poor condition of the float glass market.
Luoyang's current price earnings ratio was around 26.6 and 24.1 times for 1996 and 1997 based on Salomon's forecast.
"Our target price (is) revised down to a buy below HK$0.50 from HK$1," Lau said in a recent report. Luoyang ended at HK$1.39 on Wednesday.

Tsingtao Brewery, which was seen in a turnaround situation, achieved an 8.0 percent growth on interim profit but upgrades of production facilities were expected to lower production volume growth in the second half of 1996, the report said.

Salomon said Tsingtao's earnings growth would come primarily from higher production while operating margin would continue to be squeezed. It cut profit estimates to 105 million yuan from 125 million in 1996 and to 125 million from 154 million in 1997.

Salomon cut profit forecast of Yizheng to 503 million from 1.01 billion in 1996 and 780 million from 966 million in 1997 as high depreciation and operating cost and weak prices due to oversupply dampened chemical companies in China.
"A one percent decline in Yizheng's product prices results on a three percent decline in net profit," Lau said.
The average selling price of Yizheng fell 31.76 percent in the first half of the year, which caused a 75 percent decline in interim net to 212 million in 1996.
But Salomon said Yizheng was one of the better H shares plays to take advantage of a recovery in the chemical sector, recommending a buy below HK$1.50. Yizheng closed at HK$1.81 on Wednesday.

Lau put Jilin's net profit at 658 million and 691 million yuan for 1996 and 1997, respectively. Salomon recently downgraded the company to underperform from a hold on higher oil cost and lower profit margins in the second half of 1996.

Salomon maintained its profit forecast in Shanghai Petrochemical of 1.78 billion yuan for 1996 and 1.50 billion for 1997 but it would only recommend a buy when the share fell to below HK$1.65. Shanghai Petrochem ended at HK$1.99 on Wednesday.
